title: Qt: Use a vertical layout with Lua console
description:
Switch from a horizontal input/output text layout to a vertical
layout with a splitter in the middle.

Change to a QTextEdit while at it, just because the performance
reasons that might suggest using QPlainTextEdit are not very
relevant here.

Use the proper keyboard shortcut for macOS.

MR !11734 fixes the dialog geometry, can you check if it also fixes this crash for you?

And if the Keyboard shortcut is correctly represented with `QKeySequence::toString()` on macOS while at it.

The problem here is that the console menu is registered multiple times when doing reload Lua plugins, but never deregistered/cleared. This is why the invalidated `L` is still used in different places.

My suggestion is to revert the "Close console dialog when reloading Lua" commit and change the logic in `wslua_init()` to update all console menus with a new `L` instead of always doing `funnel_register_console_menu()`. By doing this we should be able to reload Lua plugins and keep the console open. `wslua_init()` already know if `first_time`.

We don't really need to pass the Lua state to the dialog, since it is already a global variable.
But the print function still needs special handling during reinitialization with an open dialog window.

I didn't consider the Lua state could be reloaded when I started with this, I'll keep working on it. There should only ever be single dialog instance too. That needs to be fixed.
The main_window_slots code is duplicated for Logray, do you need to fix the issue for both?

Actually I was hoping we could keep the Console dialog when reloading Lua plugins, because this would be a great improvement when creating and debugging Lua scripts. We already got some user requests about this.

commits_data.message:
Rename the Lua log domain

The name "WSLua" looks kind of weird. Use just "Lua" instead.

commits_data.title: Qt: Close console dialog when reloading Lua
commits_data.message:
Qt: Close console dialog when reloading Lua

Fixes a crash using the console because the dialog holds a pointer
to the Lua state that gets invalidated by the reload.

Forcing the dialog to close drops the invalid reference and avoids
the crash and all the other attending state problems with the reload.

In theory there might be console types other than Lua so we may
want to fix the code to close only Lua type dialogs if only Lua
plugins are reloaded.
